issues.description: Window bays exhibit uniform procedural repetition across south and north facades.
Ground floor interior lacks structural partitions; functions are blurred in an open hall cavity.
Workshop equipment is incomplete; missing essential blacksmith tools such as anvil, blast furnace, and grindstone.
Main residential entrance lacks focal hierarchy over secondary service doors.

repairInstructions.expectedBenefit: Eliminates obvious procedural repetition and emphasizes functional distinction.
repairInstructions.semanticInstruction: group residential windows into paired bays and replace workshop openings with narrow forge ventilation slits

repairInstructions.expectedBenefit: Provides believable interior circulation and functional architectural zoning.
repairInstructions.semanticInstruction: partition ground floor into a dedicated blacksmith workshop, living hall, and storage pantry with interior connecting doorways

repairInstructions.expectedBenefit: Enhances thematic narrative and visual interior richness.
repairInstructions.semanticInstruction: equip the workshop zone with blast furnace, anvil, grindstone, water quenching cauldron, and raw material storage

repairInstructions.expectedBenefit: Clarifies building circulation and adds focal depth to the primary facade.
repairInstructions.semanticInstruction: establish clear entrance hierarchy with a prominent timber-framed porch canopy for the residence and a separate utilitarian door for the workshop

strengths: Believable asymmetrical massing with primary living hall and attached secondary workshop wing.
Prominent stone forge chimney rising above the asymmetrical roofline with campfire smoke aesthetic.
Multi-layer facade depth relief with prominent timber columns framing recessed plank bays.
